item.research_question: How does the presence of preexisting helium (0%, 1%, and 2%) affect defect evolution, specifically dislocation loop formation and bubble growth, in equimolar WTaCrV high-entropy alloy compared to pure tungsten under overlapping displacement cascades mimicking fusion-relevant neutron irradiation?
item.material_system: Equimolar WTaCrV high-entropy alloy (W:Ta:Cr:V = 1:1:1:1) and pure Tungsten (W)
item.processing_route: Classical molecular dynamics simulations using LAMMPS with EAM potentials; 550 overlapping displacement cascades with 10 keV recoil energy to reach 0.2 dpa at 300 K; He atoms added randomly at 1% and 2% concentrations.
item.test_conditions: Temperature: 300 K; Dose: up to 0.2 displacements per atom (dpa); Helium concentrations: 0%, 1%, and 2%; Recoil energy: 10 keV; Displacement threshold energy (Ed): 40 eV.
key_findings: In pure W, large interstitial clusters and dislocation loops formed readily, whereas WTaCrV HEA showed strong resistance to their formation.
At 0.2 dpa without He, the mean maximum interstitial cluster size in pure W was approximately 26 times larger than that in the WTaCrV alloy.
Introducing 1% He increased the Frenkel pair concentration in W by approximately five times, while in WTaCrV HEA it increased by only 1.5 times.
In W with 2% He, a large polygonal interstitial network developed, reaching a size of up to 12,869 atoms at 0.2 dpa.
No dislocation loops were observed in WTaCrV HEA even at 0.2 dpa with 2% helium content.
In WTaCrV HEA with 2% He, the majority of vacancies were concentrated in clusters ranging from 21 to 50 vacancies.
Bubble growth in WTaCrV was driven by helium trapping at vacancy sites and the coalescence of smaller bubbles, with larger bubbles remaining stable against cascade overlap.
item.mechanism: The superior resistance to dislocation loops in WTaCrV is attributed to slowed interstitial diffusion and high recombination probability of interstitials and vacancies. In contrast, bubble formation in the HEA is driven by the high binding energy of vacancies to He clusters (1–2 eV for n > 2) and low He diffusivity, which limits He mobility and promotes trapping at vacancy sites. In W, helium stabilizes defects and modifies local stress fields, facilitating dislocation loop rafting and the formation of polygonal interstitial networks.
item.limitations: The study is limited to molecular dynamics simulations at 300 K and does not cover high-temperature behavior or long-term experimental validation under dual-beam irradiation conditions.
item.future_work: The authors suggest the necessity of revisiting the design principles for HEAs to achieve better radiation resistance under complex irradiation environments where bubble formation is a concern.
quotes: In W, dislocation loops and large interstitial clusters formed readily, with increasing He content leading to higher dislocation densities and the formation of polygonal interstitial networks.
In contrast, WTaCrV alloy exhibited strong resistance to formation of dislocation loops and large interstitial clusters but was more susceptible to bubble formation at higher He concentrations.
Bubble growth was driven by helium trapping at vacancy sites and the coalescence of smaller bubbles.
